question: Does the preprint's DNg100 rate model, built by the preprint's rules from our maleCNS wiring, produce the DNg100 front-left motor rhythm?
reference: Pugliese, Tuthill, Brunton et al. 2025, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944 (preprint); Methods text read 2026-11-06. b and the functional form from fly-brain-main/src/ratenet.js (the preprint's equation is an image).
not_claimed: that our LIF engine is wrong
any change to the live engine, calibration or mappings

sources.cache: maleCNS cache (load_cache verifies the canonical source fingerprints)

network.rule: 68 V1 front-left MNs (bodymap ' T1 left'); every non-MN neuron with >= 5 synapses onto them; every descending neuron with >= 5 synapses onto a non-DN premotor neuron; non-MN neurons with transmitter 'unknown' removed; edges >= 5 synapses within the network
network.amendment_before_any_simulation: The design removed every unknown-transmitter neuron. Running the network description (structure only) showed this would drop 21 of the 68 scored MNs. MNs are therefore kept as readout regardless of transmitter; an unknown-transmitter MN sends no input (sign 0). 25 non-MN unknown neurons are removed.
network.signs: acetylcholine +1; gaba, glutamate, histamine -1; dopamine, serotonin, octopamine +1 (ratenet.js modulatorySign 1); unknown 0

model.equation: tau_i dr_i/dt = max(rmax_i tanh((a_i/rmax_i)(I_i + b sum_j W_ij r_j - theta_i)), 0) - r_i
model.draws: numpy.random.default_rng(seed): a* ~ N(1, 0.1), theta* ~ N(7.5, 0.6), tau ~ N(20, 2) ms, rmax ~ N(200, 10) Hz, in that order, each for all network neurons; non-positive values redrawn
model.size: a = a*/s, theta = theta*.s, s = size/542747200 (VNC-region median, region_scales); no cap
model.solver: scipy solve_ivp RK45, rtol 2e-6, atol 5e-9; r(0)=0; segments 0-20 ms (I=0) and 20-1000 ms (I_stim on the stimulated neuron); samples every 1 ms, t = 0..999
model.silencing: the silenced neuron's activation is held at 0 (its rate stays 0)

drive_adjustment: start I_stim 250; recruited = network neurons with r > 0.01 at any sample t = 250..999; < 5 -> double, > 500 -> halve, re-running the same draw; at most 10 adjustments (11 simulations); still outside [5, 500] -> INFEASIBLE (score NaN). BASELINE has no stimulus and no adjustment.

readout.trace: each front-left MN's rate at t = 250..999 ms, unsmoothed
readout.active_mn: max rate in that window > 0.01 Hz
readout.score: dng100_rhythm.rhythmicity per active MN (V1, unchanged); replicate score = mean over active MNs, NaN if none; replicate frequency = median 1000/period over active MNs with score > 0
readout.condition: score = mean over feasible replicates with a score; frequency = median over them

conditions.silenced: SIL_E1, SIL_E2, SIL_I1: DNg100_L stimulated, one core cell silenced, seeds 1-64 each, own adjustment

controls.rule: 20 acetylcholine descending neurons in the network other than DNg100_L/R, drawn without replacement by numpy.random.default_rng(20261107).choice from the sorted dense indices

acceptance.C1_rhythm: DNG100 score >= 0.5 AND > 80th percentile of the feasible control scores
acceptance.C3_necessity: SIL_E1, SIL_E2 and SIL_I1 each score < 0.5 (no feasible replicate counts as abolished)
acceptance.RATE_RHYTHM_PARTIAL: C1 and (not C2 or not C3)
acceptance.INCONCLUSIVE: source, network or control mismatch; I2/I3 test failure; or no feasible DNG100 replicate

integrity.I1_sources: file hashes, network body-ID hash and control draw checked at run start
integrity.I4_completeness: 592 replicates, each with seed, status and drive history

reported_not_gated: per-MN score, period and rates with muscle names
Ti flexor vs Ti extensor cross-correlation lag

expectations.note: recorded before any protocol simulation; wrong ones are recorded as wrong

plumbing_disclosure: One timing replicate (DNg100_L, seed 0, not a protocol seed) was run before registration and read only for wall time; its output also printed the number of simulations used by the adjustment rule (3). Cost: about 0.1 s per replicate. The design's no-drive timing replicate was not informative (all rates stay 0), so a driven one was used.
execution: one command (--run equivalent: --output) runs all 592 replicates and computes the verdict in the same process, as Stage 1 V1 did; output opened exclusively; run once.
interpretation_limits: Reconstruction, not the authors' code: b and the nonlinearity from ratenet.js; 'recruited' read as active network neurons; 64 replicates instead of 1,024.
Different connectome and MN set: 68 bodymap MNs (21 with unknown transmitter, kept as readout) versus 144 MANC fl MNs.
Rate model: no spikes, delays or adaptation. Isolated network: no brain, other legs or sensory feedback.
Neural only: no body, physics, gait or balance; no motor coordinate status change (20/42 admitted, +4 conditional).
single_run: Run once after protocol, code and tests are committed and pushed; no seeds, thresholds, windows or parameters changed after seeing results.
